title: Harmonize credential handshake and stream interfaces across SDKs; introduce auth-backoff-presets and bump versions
author: Anika Patel
commits: b1a2c3d: introduce auth-backoff-presets and initial orchestrator shim
d4e5f6a: unify handshake payload shape across SDKs (timestamp, nonce, ttl)
a7b8c9d: add explicit reconnect semantics and cancelable pullstream handle
e1f2a3b: tests: add cross-sdk integration tests for rotation and resume
c3d4e5f: docs: migration guide and changelogs
f6e7d8c: ci: add SDK integration stage and version bump script
description: Context: We have drift between the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs in how credential handshakes are performed and how streaming consumers handle reauth+resume. That drift causes intermittent production incompatibilities (notably stale TTL handling and non-deterministic resume behavior) and increases maintenance surface when runtime routing falls back between model variants. Summary of change: this PR unifies the credential handshake contract (canonical payload keys: nonce, issued_at_iso, ttl_seconds, signature_v1), introduces a small auth-backoff-presets library consumed by all three SDKs (fast/medium/strict profiles), and standardizes stream handle ergonomics to support explicit Cancel(), Resume(), and Heartbeat() hooks. What changed (high level): - New orchestrator shim implemented in redwood-sdk-typescript/src/auth/credential_orchestrator.ts used as canonical reference. - Python and Go adopt the same handshake payload shape and validate signatures using shared test vectors. - Pullstream/push/pipeline handles expose Cancel/Resume/Heartbeat methods with consistent semantics and error codes (SDK_ERR_AUTH_EXPIRED, SDK_ERR_STREAM_ABORTED). - Introduced auth-backoff-presets with deterministic jittered backoffs that are safe for short-lived badges (recommended for hosted API) and long-lived leases (recommended for Dedicated/Private). - Added cross-language integration tests that run against the local integration harness to assert rotation+resume behavior under network partitions. Compatibility & migration notes: - Backwards compatible: servers that accept previous handshake fields will continue to operate, but clients built on the new SDKs will now send the canonical fields. - Operators should ensure their token rotation service returns signature_v1 when rotating tokens; a migration guide is included at docs/migration-guides/sdk-auth-migration.md. - Version bumps: python -> 1.9.0, typescript -> 1.12.0, go -> 1.5.3. Rollout plan: - Merge to main guarded by CI integration stage. - Publish SDK packages with staged rollout to avoid simultaneous client churn. - Monitor auth.* and stream.resume.* metrics in the Redwood Console; alert if error rate increases > 0.5% from baseline. Testing: unit tests for each SDK, cross-sdk integration tests for rotation/resume, stress job that simulates 1k clients reconnecting. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-3421) [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] docs and migration guide [x] changelogs updated [x] version bump script included Related: ENG-3421, SDK-1287, SUP-421.
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Left a request - please add a small test that verifies signature_v1 absent fallback path (server accepts legacy token).
Anika Patel: Added the fallback test and a short note in the migration guide, pushed in commit e1f2a3b.

Sofia Martin: Confirmed ergonomics for pullstream.Resume() look good. Suggested clearer naming for Cancel -> Abort. Updated in TS and Go; Python retains cancel() naming but exported alias abort() added for parity.

Diego Morales: Ran the integration stage locally, observed transient flakiness in the stress harness tied to heartbeat frequency. Tuned default heartbeat to 15s in auth-backoff-presets and re-ran CI; all green.
release_notes: SDKs: Unify credential handshake payload and stream handle ergonomics; add auth-backoff-presets to improve reauth stability. Bumped versions: python 1.9.0, typescript 1.12.0, go 1.5.3. See migration guide for minor server compatibility details.
notes_for_backport: If backporting to the previous release branch, include the tests and changelogs but omit the version bump script; be cautious about the heartbeat default change (15s).
